accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 3-LS4-2 and its clarification statement (variations among individuals of a species may give advantages in surviving, finding mates and reproducing; examples: plants with larger thorns are less likely to be eaten, animals with better camouflage are more likely to survive and leave offspring) and the DfE Year 6 Evolution and inheritance statements (offspring vary and are not identical to their parents; adaptation may lead to evolution). The model is kept true at this level: birds remove the most visible individuals (hunt() removes the 4 beetles whose shade is furthest from the ground's), only survivors reproduce, offspring resemble parents (breed() scales survivor counts back to 12), and a no-predator year leaves the mix unchanged. Simulation values recomputed: start [2,3,2,3,2]; dark soil survivors [0,1,2,3,2], pale sand survivors [2,3,2,1,0]; generations [0,1,3,5,3] → [0,0,0,7,5] → [0,0,0,4,8]. Peahen choice of showy males is from Petrie (1994); stretching not being inherited is the standard rejection of Lamarckian inheritance. Parameterised answers 12−p, 2n, 12−d and 3s are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented natural-selection misconceptions (Bishop and Anderson, 1990; Nehm and Reilly, 2007): all members of a species are identical (prediction step 1, m1, challenge same/babies), need- or effort-driven change (challenge try, choose, weather; p5 'the beetles decide to turn dark'), inheritance of characteristics acquired in life (giraffe stretch: m3, challenge lamarck/daily), one feature is best everywhere (pale sand hunt, place cards, m5, challenge always/night), survival as strength (challenge strong), and change happening without selection (no-birds control year, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagvary models this topic's own mechanism: measuring variation within one species on a dot plot, a predation hunt whose survivors depend on ground colour, a generation-by-generation breeding run with a shade histogram and a no-predator control, a difference-to-advantage matcher (food reach, warmth, defence, mate choice) and a habitat-dependence sorter. It differs from flagcamo (529, background matching for individual animals, no generations), flagtrait (680, offspring resemble parents) and flagadapt (adaptations); none simulate selection across generations. The lab_distinct gate passes under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is found by doing before the text states it: measuring the six beetles fills a dot plot from 11 to 15 mm; running the same 12 beetles on two grounds shows the caught shade flip, so the learner sees that the advantage depends on the habitat; three generations on dark soil push the histogram to the dark end, and the no-birds button shows the mix does not move without a predator; matching and place cards extend the idea beyond colour. Step summaries appear only when each task is complete.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: whether all beetles of one kind are exactly the same (Yes tempts; the measurements differ), which beetles birds catch most on dark soil (The dark ones tempts for learners who think darker means easier to see; the hunt removes the palest), and what most beetles look like after three generations (The same mix as at the start tempts; the histogram shifts to dark). A.reveal echoes the locked-in choice on completion.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each and twelve distinct messages (same, babies, try, strong, lamarck, daily, always, night, choose, weather, vanish, nochange), e.g. lamarck: 'Changes during a life, like stretching, are not passed to the young. Giraffes born with longer necks pass those on.' In-lab misses also name the slip: running a second hunt on the same ground, sending birds before choosing a ground, matching a difference to another's advantage ('"Stays warm in a cold winter" belongs to a different difference. A longer neck reaches high leaves…'), and sorting a place card the wrong way with the reason.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits: kid paragraphs at about FK grade 1–3 (overall 2.0) and adult text at about grade 7.6 after a first-pass rewrite (the first draft read at 11.7). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Babies look like their parents.'), and the precise words are used and explained: variation, kind (species), advantage, survive, generation, habitat, camouflage idea (stands out / hard to see).

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches and explanation overlap with every other lesson is under 12%. Each step has one job (variation, predation, inheritance across generations, other advantages, habitat dependence), and every feedback line carries a count, a feature or a reason. Item explanations give the mechanism rather than restating the answer.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark on every step, before and after Show me. First-pass fixes: the habitat bins listed every sorted card in tiny text that overflowed (now a card count), the survivor tally was white text on pale sand (now on a dark pill below the ground), the hunt banner ran to three lines (shortened), the matched-differences summary ran off the canvas (now one wrapped card per line), and the generations step called the start 'Generation 0' (now 'Starting group'). Beetles are drawn large enough to see each shade; every action also has a full-size button; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.

accessibility.evidence: Everything is doable with buttons: Measure beetle 1–6, Dark soil, Pale sand and Send the birds / Reset, Next generation and No birds this year, one button per advantage, and the two habitat boxes, each with an aria-label where the text alone is unclear. The canvas aria-label reports measurements, the beetle mix by shade, survivors and progress after every action, and challenge feedback is an aria-live status. Colour is never the only cue: shades are named in text (very pale to very dark) and survivors are counted in words. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
